text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An aide of opposition FORD-Asili party Chairman Kenneth Matiba says the party will go ahead with preparations for the general elections despite the chairman saying last week he would boycott them.
- The National Council of Churches of Kenya calls for a coalition government and accuses President Daniel arap Moi of reneging on a January 1995 promise for constitutional reforms.
- Kenyans appeal for an extension of voter registration.
- The Pope's envoy in Kenya says the pontiff fully backs a proposed meeting between President Moi and the head of the Roman Catholic church in Kenya to discuss political reforms.
- The treasurer of opposition National Democratic Party threatens to deregister the party unless its chairman Raila Odinga cooperates with President Moi.
- Voter registration exercise ends on Monday after a week's extension by the National Electoral Commission.
- Martin Shikuku, secretary-general of FORD-Asili party, says he hates the Kikuyu community, the most populous ethnic group in the country.
- The chairman of Maendeleo ya Wanawake, Kenya's largest women's grassroots body, says the country is not ready for a woman president.
- Efforts by Rwanda, Burundi and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to revive an old alliance -- the Economic Community of the Great Lakes -- receives short shrift from Uganda.
- A Kenya opposition weekly, The People, says it plans to challenge a record libel judgement of 10 million shillings ($181,000) awarded to an aide of President Moi.
- Tanzanian authorities say none of 220 former Zairean soldiers in the northwestern Tanzanian border region of Kigoma will be allowed to slip back home. ($1=55 Kenyan Shillings)
